To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The adoption of prepaid mobile services in the developing world is a function of the regulatory environment in the country and the stage of development of the mobile network.
prepaid mobile services are not an adequate foundation for further information services.
prepaid mobile is a poor substitute for fixed line telephony and that the development of mobile networks in a country is affected by its level of economic development.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulatory and network conditions which determine the future of mobile adoption and the potential for further information infrastructure development.
the relationship between the network, regulation, and access to future services.
the regulatory conditions that determine the future information infrastructure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
prepaid mobile is a useful addition to the network, but that the regulatory periphery is still important and needs attention.
prepaid mobile is not a good substitute for the development of a fixed infrastructure, but it is an important part of the development of a mobile infrastructure.
prepaid mobile is an efficient means of increasing teledensity, but that its use should be carefully considered in the context of future network development.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the regulatory peripheries, the places that have been ignored in regulatory development, are the most interesting and the most important to understand in terms of future development of information services.
the development of the network is crucial for economic and social development and it should be done in a way that it can be expanded to reach the whole population.
prepaid is an interesting and important phenomenon, but that it should not be seen as an end in itself.
The main takeaway from our work is that

regulatory policy needs to be more nuanced and to take a long‐term perspective, and that it should be more sensitive to regional and national differences in order to ensure that the network being established will be able to deliver the full range of information services.
prepaid is not the solution to access for all, nor is it a stepping‐stone to future information services.

regulators need to take account of the fact that mobile networks and services are developing at different rates in different parts of the country and, in the long run, this will affect the quality and extent of access to future information services.
